nuggets.text: Kamden Sixkiller is a distant relative of Sonny Sixkiller, the famous Washington quarterback of the early 1970s.
The Fighting Camels' first-ever meeting with the Gators is also the program's first game against an SEC opponent.
The Fighting Camels held Western Carolina to one rushing yard, the fewest they have ever allowed a nonconference opponent.
The Fighting Camels' home opener was pushed to Sunday after lightning and a malfunctioning stadium light bank.
The Fighting Camels have beaten two ranked FCS teams in program history, and both were Western Carolina.
Braxton Harris played quarterback at Mary Hardin-Baylor and reached the 2004 Division III national championship game.
Legend says the Fighting Camels nickname came from 'Your name's Campbell; then get a hump on you!' being misheard as 'camel.'
The Fighting Camels have two camel mascots, Gaylord and Gladys.
The Fighting Camels' opener at ETSU was the 100th road game of their modern era, which began in 2008.
Kamden Sixkiller threw for 343 yards in the opener at ETSU, the sixth-most passing yards in a game in Campbell history.
